chapter_title: Concept of Mole and Chemical Calculation

sections.content_markdown:
**Problem:** $75\text{ g}$ chlorine gas is mixed with $5\text{ g}$ hydrogen gas. Which is the limiting reactant here? How much of which reactant will be left over at the end of the reaction?

$$\text{H}_2 \quad + \quad \text{Cl}_2 \quad \longrightarrow \quad 2\text{HCl}$$
$$2\text{ gram} \quad \quad 2 \times 35.5\text{g} = 71\text{ gram} \quad \quad 2 \times 36.5\text{g} = 73\text{ gram}$$

**Solution:** The equation of the reaction tells:

$2\text{ gram}$ hydrogen gas needs $71\text{ gram}$ chlorine in the reaction

So, $5\text{ gram}$ hydrogen gas needs in the reaction $\frac{71 \times 5}{2} = 177.5\text{ gram}$ chlorine

Since only $75\text{ gram}$ chlorine is given for the reaction, so $\text{Cl}_2$ will finish itself earlier and it is the limiting reactant.
**Task:** Find out how much $\text{H}_2$ is left over in the above reaction.

sections.section_title: Calculation of the Percentage of Yield
sections.content_markdown:
The reactants used in chemical reactions are not always found as $100\%$ pure. The purest chemical substances / reactants are called Analar or Analar grade substance. Analar substances are $99\%$ pure. The impure substances are purified through crystallization, distillation, fractional distillation, chromatography etc processes which you will learn about in higher classes.

Many a times, one or more purification process fails to yield $100\%$ pure products. When the reactant is not $100\%$ pure, the reaction does not yield the amount of product that was calculated from the amount of limiting reactant.
